text: Target blood sugar levels before meals for adults with diabetes are generally between 80-130 mg/dL (4.4-7.2 mmol/L). Post-meal targets (1-2 hours after eating) should be under 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L).

If blood sugar drops below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), follow the 15-15 rule: consume 15 grams of fast-acting carbs (e.g., 4 oz fruit juice or 3-4 glucose tablets), wait 15 minutes, and recheck blood sugar.

Glycemic Index (GI) measures how rapidly a carbohydrate food turns into glucose. Low GI foods (<=55) digest slowly and cause gradual rises in blood sugar, while high GI foods (>=70) spike glucose rapidly.

Physical activity increases insulin sensitivity, allowing muscles to absorb glucose even without extra insulin. Blood sugar can continue dropping up to 24 hours after moderate to high intensity workouts.
